{"uid":"74jsLx2EA","markdown":"- MCP node format: CrossApp now or JSON-LD now? (analysis for team review) <roam uid="74jsLx2EA" refs="4"/>
  - The question <roam uid="ufhC1l8By" heading="3"/>
    - [Decision 5](((5uE6qRwD7))) of the [headless MCP retrieval spec](((igzkQFr4r))) says the retrieval API and the MCP return nodes in the CrossApp format, identified by RID. CrossApp was designed as an internal format, for the plugins to talk to the database. Our long-term goal is that everything Discourse Graphs exposes to the outside is JSON-LD, so that DG graphs are part of the Linked Open Data web. <roam uid="gDCmgsF1k"/>
      - {{[[DONE]]}} [[+Marc-Antoine Parent]] hii just fyi the latest version is ((igzkQFr4r))<ref>OpenSpec v2 for Headless MCP retrieval</ref>. and the section most relevant to this discussion is ((5uE6qRwD7))<ref>5. Nodes are CrossApp nodes, identified by 'rid'</ref>. Doesn't invalidate what you're mentioning here tho just fyi on moving forward so we're all at the latest change. Once we Github sync our openSpec hopefully this won't happen anymore <roam uid="RTP8Irq6j"/>
        - Made a few changes to links, thank you! <roam uid="0EGBX-be-"/>
    - So: should the MCP start with CrossApp and switch to JSON-LD later, or start with JSON-LD? This note explains the two formats, the identifier question that the choice depends on, and the costs and benefits of each path. <roam uid="fazttu8hB"/>
  - The two formats <roam uid="vK7Wd-Pvs" heading="3"/>
    - **CrossApp** is a plain JSON format defined in TypeScript (`packages/database/src/crossAppContracts.ts`). The plugins and node discovery already use it. Its field names (`nodeType`, `content.direct`, `authorId`) mean what our code says they mean, and nothing outside our code defines them. Fields that point to other things hold IDs, not names, so the spec adds extra fields for agents: the type's name, the author's name, a source link. <roam uid="shlo3X7Tj"/>
    - **JSON-LD** is also JSON. Any JSON tool can read it. The difference is a small mapping, the context, that ties each key to a term defined on the web. For example, `title` maps to `http://purl.org/dc/terms/title`, a term that libraries, search engines and knowledge graphs already understand. Every node and every reference is named by a global identifier, so data from different sources about the same thing can be merged. A JSON-LD exporter and importer exist on the `mira-collab` branch (`apps/website/app/utils/conversion/jsonld.ts` and `fromJsonLd.ts`). They are not on `main` yet. <roam uid="_p3vjJowP"/>
  - Why JSON-LD is the goal <roam uid="iDFLrFJEb" heading="3"/>
    - **The meaning is published, not implied by our code.** A consumer doesn't need our TypeScript types to know what a field means. The context says it, using shared vocabularies (Dublin Core, PROV, SIOC) and our own `dg_core` and `dg_base` ontologies. <roam uid="PMmIQfaHj"/>
    - **Data merges across sources.** Because identifiers are global, a DG node, a MIRA record and a dataset in someone else's knowledge graph can refer to each other and combine without custom joining code. <roam uid="-bCvKe9lR"/>
    - **It reaches tools we will never integrate one by one.** Triple stores, SPARQL endpoints, library and repository systems, FAIR tooling and search engines all read RDF, and JSON-LD is one way of writing RDF. <roam uid="akcV3FsRm"/>
    - **It can change without breaking consumers.** A vocabulary grows by adding terms and stating that two terms are equivalent. A plain JSON format changes by renaming or reshaping fields, which breaks whoever built on it. <roam uid="hDCak0kvy"/>
    - **Agents can read it.** Compact JSON-LD looks like ordinary JSON with a few `@` keys. Agents already know the common vocabularies, so `dct:created` or `prov:wasDerivedFrom` need no explanation. <roam uid="Rlft3uIfc"/>
    - **One format across platforms and transports.** The same ontology is used for MIRA, and the ATProto linked-data proposal applies the same pattern to records published over other protocols. A DG node would look the same wherever it is published. <roam uid="VevnRaKhG"/>
    - The costs of JSON-LD in general: vocabulary choices become public commitments, the tooling (LDO typings, SHACL validation) is less familiar to the team than Zod, and the output is a little more verbose. <roam uid="g6X5B7vZe"/>
  - Node identity: settled for both paths <roam uid="I3tYFeIzX" heading="3"/>
    - Identity is the part that is hard to change later: once outside users or agents store a node's ID, changing it breaks their data. So it needs to be settled before either path ships. <roam uid="NMoYCk4kn"/>
    - **The RID stays the node's identity.** A RID is built from the space's URI and the node's local ID (for example, a Roam block uid). Plugins can build it offline, without asking the database, and it doesn't depend on any server. Relation triples and discovery already use it. <roam uid="LPHIH4oI0"/>
    - **Today's JSON-LD uses database IDs, which is not stable enough.** The exporter on `mira-collab` names each node with a URL built from its `Concept.id`, the database row ID. That ID changes if a node is deleted and synced again, or if the database is rebuilt or moved. Anyone who stored the URL would then hold a dead link. <roam uid="uyypzjykV"/>
    - **The proposed replacement: a web address built from the RID.** In the JSON-LD view, each node gets an HTTPS address computed from its RID, with no database lookup: <roam uid="_DfCCRmkk"/>
      - `https://discoursegraphs.com/api/data/<platform>/<space key>/<local ID>#it` <roam uid="2vngPUz97"/>
      - `<space key>` is the platform's short name for the space: the Roam graph name, or the Obsidian vault ID. <roam uid="sdgB4T1xG"/>
      - Fetching the address (without `#it`) returns the node's description directly, with no redirect. <roam uid="5pdjrzejB"/>
      - `#it` separates the node itself from the document that describes it, which is standard practice in linked data. <roam uid="XYyYz5_JB"/>
      - Each node in the JSON-LD also carries its RID explicitly. Then anyone holding a RID (a plugin, an agent, CrossApp data) can match nodes by comparing strings, without reimplementing the address rules. <roam uid="-SlrsZ4si"/>
      - Node types get the same treatment, using the type's RID. <roam uid="eZ7H3CbvP"/>
    - The RID is the node's identity, and the web address is a second way of writing the same identity for the linked-data web. They are not two identities. <roam uid="AUztwWBA8"/>
    - **Still open:** which property links a node's web address to its RID. The candidates are `owl:sameAs`, `dct:identifier`, or a property of our own. This doesn't affect the comparison below. <roam uid="TXZMHDdWw"/>
    - Note: This is mirroring [something](https://github.com/MIRA-science/linkedopendata-at/blob/main/atproto-linked-data-proposal.md) I'm proposing for ATProto in general <roam uid="0WL--pbRD"/>
  - Proposed route layout (recommendation for team review) <roam uid="bzuaL-NVQ" heading="3"/>
    - [[>]] [[!WARNING]] Recommendation, not a decision\nThis section changes the route table in the headless MCP retrieval spec, so it needs the team's review, and Trang's in particular. <roam uid="CPbHBmb72"/>
    - **The problem.** Two route designs serve CrossApp today, and neither is implemented: <roam uid="uRqmIDbGB"/>
      - [The July 9 route plan](((1OhxQeTEs))): `/api/internal/space/[space_id]/concept/[id]` and `/api/internal/space/[space_id]/content`, RESTful and keyed by database IDs. <roam uid="11Ngdh8KK"/>
      - [The retrieval spec](((uKfGP4DSF))): `/api/v1`, with four operations for the MCP (get a node, search, list node types, discourse context). Get-node is `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}`. <roam uid="19MlzvNLN"/>
    - We should have one family of CrossApp routes, not two. Both designs also have a problem with the identifier in the path: <roam uid="Fb3zVjYEq"/>
      - The July plan uses database IDs, which we don't want to give out (see "Node identity"). <roam uid="FGvOPKsk2"/>
      - A RID contains `/` and `:`, and Roam RIDs also contain `#`. As one path segment, it must be percent-encoded, or everything after the `#` never reaches the server. <roam uid="YT-1uZl8L"/>
    - **What the path should say.** Two things are true of these routes, and the path should say both: <roam uid="IuPM0EFew"/>
      - **They are internal.** CrossApp is not the public data format, and nobody outside DG should build on it. The `internal` segment says this to any developer who looks at the traffic. <roam uid="nSuj0_sDj"/>
      - **They are versioned.** The MCP is installed from npm, and the plugins run in users' graphs and vaults. Old copies of both keep calling the routes for months. So the routes are a contract with clients we shipped and can't update, even if only our own clients use them. A `v1` segment says this. <roam uid="FamyXrNNH"/>
    - `/api/v1` alone reads as "the DG API" and invites outside use. `/api/internal` alone suggests we can change the routes at any time. Together, `/api/internal/v1/...` says both true things. <roam uid="LQqBLnAMH"/>
    - **Recommended layout.** Use the same path suffix as the JSON-LD addresses: `<platform>/<space key>/<local ID>`. <roam uid="uOMpUz5Ar"/>
      - {{[[table]]}} <roam uid="n7bw9McIk"/>
        - **Operation** <roam uid="miW-EAR-J"/>
          - **Route** <roam uid="MavQBljPP"/>
        - Get a node <roam uid="1HT4WTp4Q"/>
          - `GET /api/internal/v1/<platform>/<space key>/<local ID>` <roam uid="BbY5xt2s6"/>
        - Discourse context of a node <roam uid="zbtx9A3Wu"/>
          - `GET /api/internal/v1/<platform>/<space key>/<local ID>/context` <roam uid="Wby4xMZkT"/>
        - Search <roam uid="8JxAYXJOk"/>
          - `POST /api/internal/v1/search` <roam uid="jhLTdFWo4"/>
        - List node types <roam uid="TP6EF48dL"/>
          - `GET /api/internal/v1/types` <roam uid="Lr5fY8504"/>
      - The four operations of the retrieval spec stay. Routes are RESTful where a resource exists. Search is not a resource, so it stays an operation. <roam uid="nodLoDL_G"/>
      - No database IDs and no encoded RIDs appear in paths. <roam uid="5l5D_Q087"/>
      - Each node has two views whose paths differ only in prefix: `/api/internal/v1/...` returns CrossApp, and `/api/data/...` returns JSON-LD. Switching the MCP to JSON-LD later becomes a change of prefix. <roam uid="Yzdu4x5Xi"/>
      - Tools still accept and return the RID. A shared helper splits a RID into platform, space key and local ID. The JSON-LD addresses need the same helper. <roam uid="xTkU_byuH"/>
    - **The JSON-LD addresses need no version.** `/api/data/<platform>/<space key>/<local ID>` is the node's public name, not a contract shape: the vocabulary grows by adding terms, so consumers don't break. The exporter on `mira-collab` keeps the `/api/data/` prefix, with the platform added to the path. Because these are public names, the paths must stay stable once anything outside MIRA uses them. They can use content negotiation to offer JSON-LD, and HTML later if wanted. <roam uid="OX7V3b6lJ"/>
    - **Cost.** The retrieval spec's route table changes, and its get-node and context inputs move from a RID parameter to path segments. The RID-splitting helper is new, but the JSON-LD work needs it anyway. <roam uid="qv7KXfIf1"/>
  - Comparison <roam uid="4LcyMwSbV" heading="3"/>
    - {{[[table]]}} <roam uid="LwO18uKAm"/>
      - **Factor** <roam uid="We3wcxMt0"/>
        - **JSON-LD from the start** <roam uid="yEzsCNYif"/>
          - **CrossApp first, JSON-LD later** <roam uid="w4IK3oasI"/>
      - **Node identity** <roam uid="DFVQOMlRr"/>
        - Web address built from the RID, plus the RID itself <roam uid="CPu2GE1xr"/>
          - The RID, the same value the JSON-LD will carry later. IDs that agents store keep working. <roam uid="37MVxNQ6E"/>
      - **MCP schedule** <roam uid="9Q93fEQMH"/>
        - Waits on the JSON-LD work: merging `mira-collab`, the new addresses, type mapping that doesn't depend on type names, settling the text format of node bodies (HTML, markdown, or both through content negotiation), structure for search results and discourse context, removing MIRA demo leftovers <roam uid="6R1fZ5A0n"/>
          - Builds on converters already merged in ENG-1985 and ENG-2091 <roam uid="Q5DQAjOUK"/>
      - **Same format as the plugins** <roam uid="Ol1GOs2Ro"/>
        - No. Plugins and discovery use CrossApp, agents get JSON-LD. <roam uid="fhzwww9KH"/>
          - Yes. One converter, one view of a node. <roam uid="_ug0RFSH6"/>
      - **Public format** <roam uid="xGDJhABFS"/>
        - JSON-LD from the first release. Vocabulary terms become public commitments early. <roam uid="Cjyfb3qDt"/>
          - The MCP's routes publish CrossApp, with the extra agent fields. <roam uid="h7uFOh_u1"/>
      - **Others build on CrossApp** <roam uid="TcYJkwHd0"/>
        - No risk <roam uid="bx3WqHkD9"/>
          - Real risk. Users see CrossApp through the MCP and may build scripts, skills or integrations on it. If the MCP becomes a skill, the line between internal tool and public protocol blurs further. The longer the delay, the more there is to migrate or keep supporting.\n\n- {{[[DONE]]}} [[+Marc-Antoine Parent]] i would push back on the risk here. It's true that they can see the shape of the CrossApp type, but not that they can modify our internal code/ any functionalities based on the knowledge of what CrossAppType looks like. Plus in the extended datatype via MCP, I'm not exposing any PI either <roam uid="0iN7SLFV6"/>
            - The risk is for them, that they start building tooling on the CrossApp type when it leaks.  <roam uid="RQXZ2FNtJ"/>
      - **Readability for agents** <roam uid="Y67ZXnh9D"/>
        - Keys tied to published vocabularies. Types without a mapping in our ontologies show up as bare addresses until the type mapping improves. <roam uid="ucglQivAi"/>
          - Readable, but the meaning of each field is ours alone <roam uid="8S0cJ4HOg"/>
      - **Testing the JSON-LD pipeline** <roam uid="_vmiu6Kvk"/>
        - The MCP becomes its second real consumer, after MIRA <roam uid="BbOMCzjwN"/>
          - JSON-LD stays MIRA-only for longer <roam uid="C1pwR-75H"/>
      - **Tests and fixtures** <roam uid="FXlfKWEoD"/>
        - Written once, against a newer pipeline <roam uid="jvTR7VMoJ"/>
          - Written for CrossApp, then partly rewritten for JSON-LD <roam uid="0wtIdDZCQ"/>
      - **Validation** <roam uid="J-ulbnUWV"/>
        - LDO typings and SHACL <roam uid="E7fi7qr8C"/>
          - Zod, as now <roam uid="cSMM3eI8y"/>
      - **Search and context results** <roam uid="Bomv_KUgf"/>
        - Score, excerpt and one-hop context need a structure designed now, with no standard vocabulary to reuse\n\n{{[[DONE]]}} [[+Marc-Antoine Parent]] what's your estimate for this? this is the entirety of porting our schema to json-ld right?  <roam uid="pe7hNHgb4"/>
          - Ad hoc fields now, redesigned at the switch <roam uid="wuZ_tG8O6"/>
          - This should not take very long, it's basically choosing internal vocabulary. <roam uid="-GU-4pnVB"/>
      - **Switching the MCP later** <roam uid="_INUVQVwe"/>
        - Not needed <roam uid="fX2QneeRz"/>
          - Small: a new serializer. Tool descriptions mostly stay the same if the JSON-LD names the RID property `rid`. With the proposed route layout, the MCP changes only its path prefix. <roam uid="70s_1riaq"/>
      - **Risk that the switch never happens** <roam uid="z8qcZPOg5"/>
        - None <roam uid="aLH5Vt3YZ"/>
          - Real. A format that works competes with features for priority. <roam uid="R7tk9UNLf"/>
      - **Fit with the ATProto linked-data proposal** <roam uid="LrkdV7FPz"/>
        - DG becomes a working example of the pattern early <roam uid="Qr3ObHVRK"/>
          - Same, later <roam uid="BeYVOCosn"/>
  - Reading the table <roam uid="4pnctln2N" heading="3"/>
    - Because the RID is the identity in both paths, nothing in the table is impossible to undo. Two rows favour CrossApp first: the MCP schedule, and sharing one converter with the plugins. Three rows favour JSON-LD from the start: others building on CrossApp, testing the JSON-LD pipeline, and the risk that the switch never happens. Two of those three grow with the length of the delay. <roam uid="eeHv2FnAX"/>
  - If we start with CrossApp <roam uid="EthYA7GHw" heading="3"/>
    - The delay stays cheap only if: <roam uid="dSQ7Cyt0v" childrenViewType="numbered"/>
      - The RID is the ID agents see, and tools accept it as input permanently. <roam uid="tk7JkH9ua"/>
      - The JSON-LD view carries the RID on every node, including referenced nodes and node types. <roam uid="4XSpJuwzo"/>
      - The CrossApp routes are marked as internal (the proposed `/api/internal/v1/` prefix does this) and documented as the raw format, and JSON-LD is named as the public format we intend to publish. <roam uid="1XIriAJqm"/>
      - The new address scheme replaces the `Concept.id` URLs before anything outside MIRA uses them. This applies whichever path we choose. <roam uid="4KrfqaVS_"/>
      - The switch to JSON-LD gets a ticket now, with a target date, so the delay has a known length. <roam uid="3hqUCziUo"/>

    - [Decision 5](((5uE6qRwD7))) of the [headless MCP retrieval spec](((igzkQFr4r))) says the retrieval API and the MCP return nodes in the CrossApp format, identified by RID. CrossApp was designed as an internal format, for the plugins to talk to the database. Our long-term goal is that everything Discourse Graphs exposes to the outside is JSON-LD, so that DG graphs are part of the Linked Open Data web. <roam uid="gDCmgsF1k"/>
      - {{[[DONE]]}} [[+Marc-Antoine Parent]] hii just fyi the latest version is ((igzkQFr4r))<ref>OpenSpec v2 for Headless MCP retrieval</ref>. and the section most relevant to this discussion is ((5uE6qRwD7))<ref>5. Nodes are CrossApp nodes, identified by 'rid'</ref>. Doesn't invalidate what you're mentioning here tho just fyi on moving forward so we're all at the latest change. Once we Github sync our openSpec hopefully this won't happen anymore <roam uid="RTP8Irq6j"/>
        - Made a few changes to links, thank you! <roam uid="0EGBX-be-"/>
    - So: should the MCP start with CrossApp and switch to JSON-LD later, or start with JSON-LD? This note explains the two formats, the identifier question that the choice depends on, and the costs and benefits of each path. <roam uid="fazttu8hB"/>
  - The two formats <roam uid="vK7Wd-Pvs" heading="3"/>
    - **CrossApp** is a plain JSON format defined in TypeScript (`packages/database/src/crossAppContracts.ts`). The plugins and node discovery already use it. Its field names (`nodeType`, `content.direct`, `authorId`) mean what our code says they mean, and nothing outside our code defines them. Fields that point to other things hold IDs, not names, so the spec adds extra fields for agents: the type's name, the author's name, a source link. <roam uid="shlo3X7Tj"/>
    - **JSON-LD** is also JSON. Any JSON tool can read it. The difference is a small mapping, the context, that ties each key to a term defined on the web. For example, `title` maps to `http://purl.org/dc/terms/title`, a term that libraries, search engines and knowledge graphs already understand. Every node and every reference is named by a global identifier, so data from different sources about the same thing can be merged. A JSON-LD exporter and importer exist on the `mira-collab` branch (`apps/website/app/utils/conversion/jsonld.ts` and `fromJsonLd.ts`). They are not on `main` yet. <roam uid="_p3vjJowP"/>
  - Why JSON-LD is the goal <roam uid="iDFLrFJEb" heading="3"/>
    - **The meaning is published, not implied by our code.** A consumer doesn't need our TypeScript types to know what a field means. The context says it, using shared vocabularies (Dublin Core, PROV, SIOC) and our own `dg_core` and `dg_base` ontologies. <roam uid="PMmIQfaHj"/>
    - **Data merges across sources.** Because identifiers are global, a DG node, a MIRA record and a dataset in someone else's knowledge graph can refer to each other and combine without custom joining code. <roam uid="-bCvKe9lR"/>
    - **It reaches tools we will never integrate one by one.** Triple stores, SPARQL endpoints, library and repository systems, FAIR tooling and search engines all read RDF, and JSON-LD is one way of writing RDF. <roam uid="akcV3FsRm"/>
    - **It can change without breaking consumers.** A vocabulary grows by adding terms and stating that two terms are equivalent. A plain JSON format changes by renaming or reshaping fields, which breaks whoever built on it. <roam uid="hDCak0kvy"/>
    - **Agents can read it.** Compact JSON-LD looks like ordinary JSON with a few `@` keys. Agents already know the common vocabularies, so `dct:created` or `prov:wasDerivedFrom` need no explanation. <roam uid="Rlft3uIfc"/>
    - **One format across platforms and transports.** The same ontology is used for MIRA, and the ATProto linked-data proposal applies the same pattern to records published over other protocols. A DG node would look the same wherever it is published. <roam uid="VevnRaKhG"/>
    - The costs of JSON-LD in general: vocabulary choices become public commitments, the tooling (LDO typings, SHACL validation) is less familiar to the team than Zod, and the output is a little more verbose. <roam uid="g6X5B7vZe"/>
  - Node identity: settled for both paths <roam uid="I3tYFeIzX" heading="3"/>
    - Identity is the part that is hard to change later: once outside users or agents store a node's ID, changing it breaks their data. So it needs to be settled before either path ships. <roam uid="NMoYCk4kn"/>
    - **The RID stays the node's identity.** A RID is built from the space's URI and the node's local ID (for example, a Roam block uid). Plugins can build it offline, without asking the database, and it doesn't depend on any server. Relation triples and discovery already use it. <roam uid="LPHIH4oI0"/>
    - **Today's JSON-LD uses database IDs, which is not stable enough.** The exporter on `mira-collab` names each node with a URL built from its `Concept.id`, the database row ID. That ID changes if a node is deleted and synced again, or if the database is rebuilt or moved. Anyone who stored the URL would then hold a dead link. <roam uid="uyypzjykV"/>
    - **The proposed replacement: a web address built from the RID.** In the JSON-LD view, each node gets an HTTPS address computed from its RID, with no database lookup: <roam uid="_DfCCRmkk"/>
      - `https://discoursegraphs.com/api/data/<platform>/<space key>/<local ID>#it` <roam uid="2vngPUz97"/>
      - `<space key>` is the platform's short name for the space: the Roam graph name, or the Obsidian vault ID. <roam uid="sdgB4T1xG"/>
      - Fetching the address (without `#it`) returns the node's description directly, with no redirect. <roam uid="5pdjrzejB"/>
      - `#it` separates the node itself from the document that describes it, which is standard practice in linked data. <roam uid="XYyYz5_JB"/>
      - Each node in the JSON-LD also carries its RID explicitly. Then anyone holding a RID (a plugin, an agent, CrossApp data) can match nodes by comparing strings, without reimplementing the address rules. <roam uid="-SlrsZ4si"/>
      - Node types get the same treatment, using the type's RID. <roam uid="eZ7H3CbvP"/>
    - The RID is the node's identity, and the web address is a second way of writing the same identity for the linked-data web. They are not two identities. <roam uid="AUztwWBA8"/>
    - **Still open:** which property links a node's web address to its RID. The candidates are `owl:sameAs`, `dct:identifier`, or a property of our own. This doesn't affect the comparison below. <roam uid="TXZMHDdWw"/>
